The words come from the paper's own supplements: item_text is the Japanese administered wording, verbatim from S1 Fig (Original question sheet in Japanese, .s001, read via soffice --convert-to txt), and item_text_translated is the authors' own English from S2 Fig (Translation question sheet, .s002) -- hence translation_source=study_supplied. Deviations from literal transcription, all deliberate: the leading '質問N' / 'N.' numbering was stripped from item_text; the inline answer options printed on the same line as the question in S1/S2 were moved to option_text; source typos were kept (S2 Q20 'about radiation about radiation', instruction 'circle that apply'). The LIVE resp values are the authors' analysis recoding, not raw responses: Q1 (age), Q6 (years in area) and Q8 (years employed) were administered as open numeric write-ins and are stored as a 1/2 dichotomy, so their option_text is left BLANK -- the paper's Tables 1-2 label only the affirmative code ('Older than 40 years', 'Living in the area for more than 7 years', 'Has worked for more than 21 years'; all three verified as resp=2 by count) and the complementary label is nowhere published, so nothing was authored to fill it. Q5's six administered distance bands and the 4-point anchors of Q13/Q14/Q18/Q20/Q21 are stored as 2 levels; option_text for those six composes the administered anchors that fold into each code, joined with ' / ' (e.g. Q13 resp 1 = '不安を感じる / やや不安を感じる'). The 2+2 collapse boundary is INFERRED, not stated by the paper; it is supported by the endorsement rates (Q20 523/550 = 95% affirmative is implausible for the strongest anchor alone) and by S2 Fig, which itself renders those items as a 4-point Yes/Probably/Probably no/No and Q5 as a bare within-30km Yes/No/I do not know. Whether Q5's 'わからない' respondents fell into code 2 is not recoverable. Q7 (2/3) and Q9 (4/5) are offset from the questionnaire's own 1/2 option numbering, consistent with a code frame shared with the municipal-staff arm named in the Japanese questionnaire title; both offsets are pinned by the count check. Rights: PLOS ONE article and all supplements are CC BY 4.0; the questionnaire is the authors' own ('We developed the written questionnaire for this study based on those used in previous studies'), no named commercial instrument, and no fee, no-redistribution or non-commercial clause was found or is quotable, so no block applies. Administered in Japanese to Japanese teachers and orphanage staff; neither the paper, its 9 supplements nor the raw workbooks contain a single Japanese character of item wording (checked: 0 CJK characters in .s003 and in the S7 workbook), so the English of the study's own supplement ships in the base fields under the translated_substitute fallback. MAPPING reconstructed. Chain: (1) S4 Table's 'Attachment k' IS raw column attach<k> -- its published geomin loadings reproduce column by column from the S7 workbook (dominant factor 19/20, r=0.969 over 40 loadings; the one flip is attach15, near-tied in both). (3) Applying the same order to its 13 attachment rows yields the shipped mapping, whose Survey 1 item means rank-correlate 0.924 with the Survey 2 MSM item means (permuting only the 13 attachment positions: null mean 0.575, p=0.00005 over 20000 permutations). TEXT is S2 Table's Survey 1 wording, transcribed verbatim, for the 13 items pinned by that chain; where S3's final wording differs trivially from S2's, S2's is shipped because this table IS Survey 1.
public_note: Only 13 of the 20 items carry wording: the paper's item list is not in the questionnaire's column order (it cannot even be reconciled at the set level with the 13 items the paper reports retaining, and it prints one wording twice), so the 7 items dropped before any per-item statistic was published cannot be tied to a code and ship with item_text blank. The 13 that do carry wording were matched through the paper's factor table and its Survey 2 readministration, which fixes them as a group but leaves 11 of 78 possible pairwise swaps among them unexcluded. The instrument was administered in Japanese and no Japanese wording is published anywhere in the article or its supplements, so the English shown is the study's own; the response anchors are the raw file's marks (x=0, triangle=1, circle=2), the only coding the study published.
